subtasks.title: Include directive tokenizer with boundary and existence rules
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/phase_findings.md §PHASE 1 documents that no include-resolution code exists in src/. The include directive is specified in PRD §2.3: 'A line of the form @path/to/file.md (optional leading whitespace, nothing else) is always expanded; the @path token is also honored inline anywhere on a line.' The canonical resolver should live in src/core/session-utils.ts alongside hashPRD.
2. INPUT: A raw PRD string (file contents) and the base directory (entry PRD's directory, project-root-relative). No prior subtask output consumed.
3. LOGIC: Implement a tokenizer that identifies @path/to/file.md include directives per PRD §2.3. Two conditions for expansion: (1) BOUNDARY — the @ is at line start (after optional whitespace) OR preceded by a non-path character (inline tokens); foo@bar.com and mid-word @ stay literal; (2) EXISTENCE — the path resolves to an existing file. Ordinary prose @mentions that don't resolve stay verbatim and silent. Create function signature: resolveIncludes(content: string, baseDir: string, opts?: ResolveOpts): Promise<string>. Add config constants PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH (default 10) and PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS (optional) to src/config/constants.ts.
4. OUTPUT: Exported resolveIncludes function in src/core/session-utils.ts, and new config constants in src/config/constants.ts. Consumed by P1.M1.T1.S2.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Add JSDoc on resolveIncludes; add PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH and PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS to .env.example; add a 'Distributed PRDs' subsection to docs/CONFIGURATION.md. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Recursive expansion engine with cycle detection and max depth
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/phase_findings.md §PHASE 1 confirms resolution base is project-root-relative (relative to the ENTRY PRD's directory, regardless of which file contains the directive). Expanded recursively with cycle detection up to PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH (default 10).
2. INPUT: resolveIncludes function and config constants from P1.M1.T1.S1. The base directory is the entry PRD's directory; all paths in included files resolve relative to this base.
3. LOGIC: Implement recursive expansion: when an include directive's file is read, its contents are themselves scanned for include directives and expanded. Maintain a visited Set<string> for cycle detection (absolute paths). Track depth and abort if exceeding PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH. The resolution base is ALWAYS the entry PRD's directory (not the including file's directory) per PRD §2.3. Create the main entry point: resolvePRD(prdPath: string, opts?: ResolveOpts): Promise<string> which reads the entry file, then calls the recursive resolver. ResolveOpts should include markers flag and maxDepth override.
4. OUTPUT: Exported resolvePRD function in src/core/session-utils.ts. Consumed by P1.M1.T1.S3 and P1.M1.T2.S1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on resolvePRD documenting recursive expansion, cycle detection, and the project-root-relative base invariant. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Idempotency guarantee, optional markers, and stale-include warnings
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PRD §2.3 mandates idempotency: 'Re-resolving already-resolved content MUST yield identical bytes.' This is the property that guarantees hash/snapshot consistency. When PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS is set, resolved output emits <!-- @include: path --> / <!-- @end-include -->. A .md token that fails to resolve MUST emit a stderr warning.
2. INPUT: resolvePRD function from P1.M1.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Ensure resolvePRD is idempotent — re-resolving its own output yields identical bytes. This means resolved content must NOT contain unexpanded @path tokens that would re-trigger expansion. Add optional markers: when PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS env is set, wrap expanded content with <!-- @include: path --> and <!-- @end-include --> comment markers. Add stale-include warning: when a .md token matches boundary rules but the path doesn't resolve to an existing file, emit a stderr warning (the token stays verbatim in output). Write comprehensive tests: idempotency (resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x)), markers toggle, stale include warning, inline vs line-start expansion.
4. OUTPUT: Completed resolvePRD with idempotency, markers, and warnings. Consumed by P1.M1.T2.S1.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on resolvePRD documenting idempotency property and marker format. This rides WITH the work.

subtasks.title: Convert ResearchQueue to depth-chained supervisor
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/phase_findings.md §PHASE 3 and signatures.md document: ResearchQueue (research-queue.ts) is a flat maxSize=3 concurrency POOL, not a depth-chain. enqueue() calls processNext() which shifts items if researching.size < maxSize. On completion, .finally removes from researching and recurses processNext. waitForPRP races RESEARCH_TIMEOUT. researchNow is synchronous inline fallback. PRD §4.2 specifies a background supervisor researching a CHAIN of up to RESEARCH_DEPTH (default 2) items ahead, prefetching the next as the orchestrator consumes each completed PRP.
2. INPUT: RESEARCH_DEPTH and PARALLEL_RESEARCH config from P3.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: Change the ResearchQueue prefetch model from flat maxSize pool to depth-chained supervisor: (a) When PARALLEL_RESEARCH is enabled, a background supervisor researches a chain of RESEARCH_DEPTH items ahead of the current item being implemented. (b) As the orchestrator consumes each completed PRP, the supervisor prefetches the next item in the chain. (c) This collapses both failure modes: 'fast implementer → stall waiting for N+1' and 'slow implementer → wasted idle capacity.' (d) The deadline via RESEARCH_TIMEOUT (now 1800s) guards each generation; a grace period precedes the heartbeat. (e) Maintain backward compatibility: when PARALLEL_RESEARCH is false, behave as today (or single-item prefetch).
4. OUTPUT: Updated ResearchQueue with depth-chained supervisor. Consumed by P3.M1.T1.S4.

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: architecture/phase_findings.md §PHASE 3 documents: stagecoach commit-message generation is one-shot and transient-API-sensitive. A generation timeout is LLM-API slowness, not a stuck subprocess — the index is left untouched + lock released on rescue. PRD §5.1 specifies retry up to COMMIT_RETRY_MAX (default 5), exponential backoff COMMIT_RETRY_DELAY (default 10s, doubling, capped 120s). Distinct from agent-subprocess timeouts (Req 3.6): watchdog kill on research/implementation/validation MUST NOT be retried; generation timeout on commit MUST be retried.
2. INPUT: Updated smartCommit with stagecoach from P3.M1.T3.S1.

(b) Wrap the stagecoach LLM commit-message generation call in a bounded retry loop using the existing retry() utility from src/utils/retry.ts. (c) The retry should use isTransientError() to distinguish API failures (retryable) from permanent errors (not retryable). (d) On each retry, the index is left untouched and any lock is released (the rescue exit behavior from PRD §5.1).
4. OUTPUT: Retry-wrapped stagecoach generation in smartCommit. Consumed by P3.M1.T4.S2.

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: PRD §4.3 specifies both classifiers MUST distinguish transient API failures (empty output, connection errors, rate limits, overloaded) from invalid model responses, retrying up to a bounded count (default 4) before giving up. On exhaustion they MUST fail to the protective/conservative default (treat as SUBSTANTIVE / DIRTY) — never silently fall through to 'could not classify' and proceed unprotected.
2. INPUT: Classifier functions from P4.M1.T1.S1.
3. LOGIC: (a) Wrap classifyChange and classifyArtifact in a bounded retry loop using retry() from src/utils/retry.ts with maxAttempts=4 (configurable). (b) Distinguish transient API failures (isTransientError → retry) from invalid model responses (parse failure → retry up to limit). (c) On exhaustion (all retries fail), return the protective/conservative default: 'SUBSTANTIVE' for change classification, 'DIRTY' for artifact classification. (d) Log a warning when falling to protective default. (e) Never return 'could not classify' — always return a protective value.
4. OUTPUT: Retry-wrapped classifiers with protective defaults. Consumed by P4.M1.T2.S1, P4.M1.T3.S1. Completes P4.M1.T1.
